description: A study of three-dimensional solids including prisms, cylinders, cones, pyramids and spheres, covering their properties, volumes and surface areas, together with slant heights, space diagonals and the angle between a line and a plane.

mcq.questionText: Find the volume of a cuboid measuring 5 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm.
mcq.explanation: The volume of a cuboid is length x width x height, so 5 x 4 x 3 = 60 cm³. Exam Tip: multiply all three dimensions for a cuboid's volume.

mcq.questionText: Find the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm (pi = 22/7).
mcq.explanation: Using V = pi r² h = (22/7) x 7 x 7 x 10 = 1540 cm³. Exam Tip: square the radius before multiplying by the height.

mcq.questionText: Find the volume of a cone of radius 6 cm and height 7 cm (pi = 22/7).
mcq.explanation: Using V = (1/3) pi r² h = (1/3) x (22/7) x 6 x 6 x 7 = 264 cm³. Exam Tip: a cone is one-third of the matching cylinder, so remember the 1/3 factor.

mcq.questionText: Find the volume of a sphere of radius 21 cm (pi = 22/7).
mcq.explanation: Using V = (4/3) pi r³ = (4/3) x (22/7) x 21 x 21 x 21 = 38808 cm³. Exam Tip: cube the radius first, then apply the 4/3 pi factor.

mcq.questionText: Find the total surface area of a cube of side 4 cm.
mcq.explanation: A cube has 6 equal square faces, so the total surface area is 6 x 4² = 6 x 16 = 96 cm². Exam Tip: a cube has 6 identical faces, so multiply one face area by 6.

mcq.questionText: Find the total surface area of a closed cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 3 cm (pi = 22/7).
mcq.explanation: Using TSA = 2 pi r(r + h) = 2 x (22/7) x 7 x (7 + 3) = 44 x 10 = 440 cm². Exam Tip: a closed cylinder includes both circular ends, so use 2 pi r(r + h).

mcq.questionText: Find the volume of a pyramid with a square base of side 6 cm and height 10 cm.
mcq.explanation: Using V = (1/3) x base area x height = (1/3) x 36 x 10 = 120 cm³. Exam Tip: find the base area first, then apply the 1/3 factor for a pyramid.

mcq.questionText: Find the curved surface area of a cone of radius 7 cm and slant height 10 cm (pi = 22/7).
mcq.explanation: Using curved surface area = pi r l = (22/7) x 7 x 10 = 220 cm². Exam Tip: the curved surface of a cone uses the slant height l, not the vertical height.

mcq.questionText: Find the surface area of a sphere of radius 7 cm (pi = 22/7).
mcq.explanation: Using SA = 4 pi r² = 4 x (22/7) x 7 x 7 = 616 cm². Exam Tip: the surface area of a sphere is 4 pi r², with no separate flat faces.

mcq.questionText: A prism has a triangular cross-section of area 20 cm² and length 12 cm. Find its volume.
mcq.explanation: The volume of a prism is cross-section area x length = 20 x 12 = 240 cm³. Exam Tip: for any prism, multiply the cross-section area by the length.

mcq.questionText: How many edges does a cuboid have?
mcq.explanation: A cuboid has 6 faces, 8 vertices and 12 edges. Exam Tip: a cuboid has 12 edges, made of 3 groups of 4 equal edges.

mcq.questionText: Find the space diagonal of a cuboid measuring 3 cm by 4 cm by 12 cm.
mcq.explanation: The space diagonal is √(3² + 4² + 12²) = √(9 + 16 + 144) = √169 = 13 cm. Exam Tip: the space diagonal of a cuboid is √(l² + w² + h²).

mcq.questionText: The angle between a line and a plane is the angle between the line and its ______ on the plane.
mcq.explanation: The angle between a line and a plane is measured between the line and its projection (its shadow) on the plane. Exam Tip: drop a perpendicular to the plane to find the projection first.

mcq.questionText: A cone has radius 6 cm and vertical height 8 cm. Find its slant height.
mcq.explanation: Using l = √(r² + h²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 cm. Exam Tip: the slant height, radius and vertical height form a right-angled triangle.

mcq.questionText: How many cubic centimetres are there in 1 cubic metre?
mcq.explanation: Since 1 m = 100 cm, 1 m³ = 100 x 100 x 100 = 1000000 cm³. Exam Tip: cube the length conversion, so 100³ = 1000000.

fib.explanation: A cube is bounded by 6 identical square faces. Exam Tip: a cube has 6 faces, 8 vertices and 12 edges.

fib.questionText: The volume of a cylinder of radius r and height h is V = ______.
fib.explanation: A cylinder's volume is the circular base area pi r² multiplied by the height h, giving pi r² h. Exam Tip: volume of a cylinder is base area times height.

fib.questionText: The volume of a cone is V = ______.
fib.explanation: A cone has one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height, so V = (1/3) pi r² h. Exam Tip: remember the 1/3 factor that separates a cone from a cylinder.

fib.questionText: The surface area of a sphere of radius r is SA = ______.
fib.explanation: The surface area of a sphere is 4 pi r², four times the area of its great circle. Exam Tip: do not confuse 4 pi r² (area) with (4/3) pi r³ (volume).
A square-based pyramid has 4 vertices around the square base and 1 apex, giving 5 vertices in total. Exam Tip: count the base corners plus the single apex.

fib.questionText: The volume of any prism equals the area of its cross-section multiplied by its ______.
fib.explanation: For a prism the cross-section is constant, so the volume is cross-section area times its length. Exam Tip: this rule works for any prism, whatever the shape of the cross-section.

fib.questionText: The volume of a cube of side 5 cm is ______ cm³.
fib.explanation: The volume of a cube is side³ = 5 x 5 x 5 = 125 cm³. Exam Tip: cube the side length to get a cube's volume.
The slant height, radius and vertical height form a right-angled triangle, so by Pythagoras l² = r² + h². Exam Tip: the slant height is the hypotenuse, so it is the largest of the three.

fib.questionText: When the curved surface of a cylinder is unrolled flat, it forms a ______.
fib.explanation: Unrolling the curved surface gives a rectangle whose length is the circumference 2 pi r and whose width is the height h. Exam Tip: the rectangle's length equals the circle's circumference.
One litre is defined as 1000 cm³, the volume of a 10 cm cube. Exam Tip: 1 litre = 1000 cm³ and 1 m³ = 1000 litres.

tf.questionText: The volume of a cone is one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height.
tf.explanation: A cone of matching base and height fills exactly one-third of the cylinder, which is why its volume formula carries the 1/3 factor.

tf.questionText: A sphere has one curved surface and no vertices or edges.
tf.explanation: A sphere is a perfectly round solid bounded by a single curved surface, with no flat faces, edges or vertices.

tf.questionText: All the faces of a cuboid are squares.
tf.explanation: A cuboid's faces are rectangles that need not be squares; only in the special case of a cube are all faces square.

tf.questionText: Doubling the radius of a sphere multiplies its volume by 8.
tf.explanation: Volume depends on r³, so doubling the radius multiplies the volume by 2³ = 8.
It has 4 edges around the square base and 4 slant edges rising to the apex, giving 8 edges in total.

tf.questionText: Total surface area is measured in cubic units.
tf.explanation: Area is measured in square units such as cm²; cubic units such as cm³ are used for volume.

tf.questionText: The volume of a hemisphere of radius r is (2/3) pi r³.
tf.explanation: A hemisphere is half a sphere, so its volume is half of (4/3) pi r³, which gives (2/3) pi r³.

tf.questionText: The space diagonal of a cube of side a has length a√3.
tf.explanation: Using √(a² + a² + a²) = √(3a²) = a√3, the space diagonal of a cube is a√3.

tf.questionText: A prism has the same cross-section throughout its length.
tf.explanation: By definition a prism has a uniform cross-section along its whole length, which is why volume equals cross-section area times length.

tf.questionText: A closed cylinder has two circular faces.
tf.explanation: A closed cylinder is sealed at both ends by a circular face, giving two circular faces plus one curved surface.

summary.correctAnswer: V = length x width x height, the product of the three perpendicular dimensions.
summary.explanation: For a cuboid 5 by 4 by 3 the volume is 5 x 4 x 3 = 60 cubic units. Exam Tip: make sure all three dimensions are in the same unit before multiplying.

summary.correctAnswer: V = pi r² h, the circular base area times the height.
summary.explanation: The base is a circle of area pi r², and stacking it to a height h gives pi r² h. Exam Tip: square the radius first, then multiply by height and pi.

summary.correctAnswer: V = (1/3) pi r² h, one-third of the matching cylinder's volume.
summary.explanation: A cone fills exactly one-third of a cylinder with the same base and height, hence the 1/3 factor. Exam Tip: use the vertical height h here, not the slant height.

summary.correctAnswer: V = (4/3) pi r³, which depends on the cube of the radius.
summary.explanation: Because the volume uses r³, doubling the radius multiplies the volume by 8. Exam Tip: cube the radius before applying the 4/3 pi factor.

summary.correctAnswer: SA = 4 pi r², four times the area of the sphere's great circle.
summary.explanation: For r = 7 with pi = 22/7 this gives 4 x (22/7) x 49 = 616 square units. Exam Tip: do not confuse 4 pi r² for area with (4/3) pi r³ for volume.

summary.questionText: Total surface area of a closed cylinder
summary.correctAnswer: TSA = 2 pi r(r + h), the curved surface plus both circular ends.
summary.explanation: The curved part is 2 pi r h and the two ends add 2 pi r², combining to 2 pi r(r + h). Exam Tip: an open cylinder drops one or both of the circular ends.

summary.correctAnswer: l² = r² + h², so l = √(r² + h²) from Pythagoras.
summary.explanation: The radius, vertical height and slant height form a right-angled triangle with l as the hypotenuse. Exam Tip: the slant height is always the longest of the three lengths.

summary.correctAnswer: V = cross-section area x length, for any uniform prism.
summary.explanation: Since the cross-section is constant along the prism, multiplying its area by the length gives the volume. Exam Tip: this works for triangular, hexagonal or any other prism shape.

summary.correctAnswer: d = √(l² + w² + h²), the longest straight line inside the cuboid.
summary.explanation: For a 3 by 4 by 12 cuboid this gives √(9 + 16 + 144) = √169 = 13 units. Exam Tip: for a cube of side a it simplifies to a√3.

summary.questionText: Angle between a line and a plane
summary.correctAnswer: The angle between the line and its projection (shadow) on the plane.
summary.explanation: Dropping a perpendicular from the line to the plane gives the projection, and the required angle sits between the line and that projection. Exam Tip: form a right-angled triangle and use tan, sin or cos to find the angle.

hoq.questionText: A closed container is made of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm topped by a hemisphere of the same radius (pi = 22/7). Find the total volume.
hoq.explanation: Cylinder volume = pi r² h = (22/7) x 49 x 10 = 1540 cm³. Hemisphere volume = (2/3) pi r³ = (2/3) x (22/7) x 343 = 718.7 cm³. Adding the parts gives 1540 + 718.7 = 2258.7 cm³. Exam Tip: break a composite solid into standard parts and add their volumes.

hoq.questionText: A cuboid has base AB = 8 cm, BC = 6 cm and height 5 cm. Find the angle between the space diagonal AG and the base, to 1 decimal place.
hoq.explanation: The projection of AG on the base is the base diagonal AC = √(8² + 6²) = √100 = 10 cm. The angle satisfies tan(angle) = height / base diagonal = 5/10 = 0.5, so the angle = 26.6°. Exam Tip: the angle to the base is measured from the diagonal's projection (the base diagonal).

hoq.questionText: A cylindrical tank has radius 1.4 m and height 2 m (pi = 22/7). Find its capacity in litres.
hoq.explanation: Volume = pi r² h = (22/7) x 1.4 x 1.4 x 2 = 12.32 m³. Converting, 12.32 m³ x 1000 = 12320 litres. Exam Tip: 1 m³ = 1000 litres, so multiply cubic metres by 1000.
